about.label: What Bizcelona is
about.h2: A business network for Barcelona founders, built around real help.
about.lede: Bizcelona is an invitation-only community for founders, independents and senior professionals who live and work in Barcelona.
paras: Most networking in this city is a room full of strangers swapping cards. Bizcelona works the other way round. Every application is read by a person, and everyone who is approved has agreed to help.

Members help each other with the things that move money: a first client, a better supplier price, a partner, a hire, a straight answer from someone who has done it. Helping is the currency here. People who give move up, and people who only take drift down.

Working for yourself in Barcelona is often a solo affair. There are no colleagues down the corridor to tell when a deal lands, and nobody to ask when something goes wrong. Bizcelona gives you those colleagues, and a group that actively champions each other’s success.
We keep it small on purpose, aiming for a core of 100 to 150 active members. A network you can actually use is smaller than one you can boast about.
notList: It is not an expensive founders’ club.
It is not a bar meetup full of people trying to sell to each other.

about.photoCaption: Barcelona from above. Every block has someone on it who could help.
about.whyNow: As AI takes over more desk work, a trusted local network of people who actually show up becomes more valuable every year.

wins.label: Celebrating wins
wins.h2: Nobody should have to celebrate a win alone.
wins.lede: Running a business in Barcelona is often a solo affair. When a deal lands, or when something goes wrong, there is nobody down the corridor to tell. Bizcelona gives you those colleagues.

moments.title: Share it in the members’ WhatsApp group
moments.body: Post your win, big or small: a first client, a signed contract, a hard month survived. Members reply, and the news lands with people who understand what it took.

moments.title: Wins get a moment at each event
moments.body: Every event makes room for members’ wins, so good news is said out loud, in the room, to the people who were there.

moments.title: Celebrated on our LinkedIn, with your permission
moments.body: With a member’s permission, we celebrate their win on Bizcelona’s LinkedIn page. Nothing is posted without your say-so.

wins.closing: Problems travel the same way. Bring a stuck one to the group, and you will find people who have been there.

timeBank.label: How members help each other
timeBank.h2: The time bank: ask for help, get a named introduction.
timeBank.lede: Need an accountant who understands freelancers, a business mentor who has scaled a company, or someone to fix your checkout? Search the skill, ask in a line or two, and we introduce you on WhatsApp.

steps.title: Search
steps.body: Look up the skill you need. You see who can help, how quickly they usually reply and how many hours they have already given.

steps.title: Ask
steps.body: Write what you need in one or two lines. Asking is free.

steps.title: Introduce
steps.body: We start a WhatsApp chat with you and the member who can help, with the context included, so nobody begins from a blank page.

steps.title: 24-hour check
steps.body: A day later we ask whether you spoke, how useful it was and roughly how long it took. The member who helped confirms you got in touch. If something went wrong, we follow up.

timeBank.note: The time bank is being introduced to members as part of the relaunch.

forWhom.label: Who it is for
forWhom.h2: Barcelona locals and newcomers, working together in English.
paras: Some members have been building in this city for years. Others landed last month and are still finding the good accountant, the right coworking space and the people worth knowing. Bizcelona puts both in the same room.
Our community language is English. Meetings and introductions happen in English, and Spanish is always welcome. You do not need to speak both.

We keep the mix of professions balanced on purpose, so no single trade fills the room. Right now we would especially like to hear from people working in SEO, web, retail, legal and tax, finance, hospitality, and trades and craft.

rules.label: House rules
rules.intro: Seven rules. They are short because we trust you to use judgement.

items.title: Give Before You Take
items.body: Share your knowledge, make introductions and offer help before you seek it yourself. Members who give freely are the ones who gain most.

items.title: Active Participation
items.body: Remain part of the conversation. Read the group, respond with care, and get in touch when you notice somebody who needs what you know. Celebrate other members’ successes: congratulate a win when you see one, and share your own. A membership that stays passive weakens what we are building.

items.title: Mutual Respect and Trust
items.body: Be professional and courteous, honour your commitments and assume good intent. What we are building is long-term relationships, not transactions.

items.title: No Unsolicited Private Messages
items.body: Ask in the group first, or already have a relationship with the person, before you send a private message. Cold outreach and sales pitches destroy trust. Introduce yourself in the group and let things develop from there.

items.title: No Promotional Posts
items.body: This is not a marketing channel. No hard selling, no adverts in disguise. If your work is relevant to a conversation, mention it naturally. Unsure? Check with an admin first. Those who repeatedly ignore this are removed.

items.title: Privacy and Confidentiality
items.body: Do not screenshot, share or republish anything from the group without permission. Treat whatever members tell you as confidential. Breaches are treated seriously.

items.title: Tiered Involvement
items.body: Not everyone takes part to the same degree, and that is fine. But everyone abides by these rules and contributes something when they do take part. If you are seldom around, ask yourself whether this is the right fit. What we want is mutual growth, not passive consumption.

partners.label: Partnerships
partners.lede: We want partners who make membership better, not logos on a banner.
partners.para: A good partner shares how we work: help first, long-term relationships, real usefulness. That might be a members-only benefit, a workshop or a shared resource. We say yes only when it is useful to members.

panels.title: Venue partners
panels.body: Co-working days move between spaces in Barcelona, and our events need a good room. If you run a space where people can work in the morning and eat lunch together, tell us about it.

panels.title: Perks and sponsors
panels.body: If you have something members would really use, such as a perk, a workshop or a resource, tell us what it is and why it helps. We only say yes to what is useful.

faq.label: Questions
faq.h2: Questions people ask before they apply.

items.a: Bizcelona is an invitation-only business networking community in Barcelona for founders, independents and senior professionals. Members help each other with real business problems, champion each other’s success, meet at a co-working day every two weeks and at least one practical event a month, often more, and ask for introductions through the time bank.

Founders, independents and senior business people who live or work in Barcelona. You need to be able to say what you do and what you can help others with. We keep the mix of professions balanced, so we read every application personally.

items.q: Why is Bizcelona by invitation, and how do I apply?
items.a: Because a network is only useful if the person you meet has been vouched for and is at your level. Apply by creating an account and telling us what you do and what you can help with. We review each application by hand before welcoming you on WhatsApp. Because of demand, approval can take up to a week.

Yes. Membership is free while we relaunch, and asking for help through the time bank is free too. We want to prove the value before we ask for payment. We will not promise a free future, and we will tell members clearly before anything changes.

items.q: What is the time bank and how does it work?
items.a: The time bank is how members help each other between events. Search for the skill you need, ask in a line or two, and we introduce you to a member on WhatsApp with the context. A day later we check whether you spoke and how useful it was.

items.q: What happens at a co-working day?
items.a: Every two weeks, members meet at a partner space in Barcelona, which changes from one day to the next. The day mixes group sessions, where members share business ideas, with focused time to get your own work done. We also go round the table: five minutes each on what you do and one problem you would like help with. Lunch is together.

We run at least one practical event a month, often more, and keep each one small enough that you can talk to everyone. Topics are hands-on, for example a beginner’s session on using AI at work. It is a few good events rather than a diary full of mixers. Dates appear on the events page.

items.q: How do members celebrate each other’s wins?
items.a: Members share wins in the members’ WhatsApp group, and every event makes a moment for them. With the member’s permission, we also celebrate wins on Bizcelona’s LinkedIn page. Running a business in Barcelona is often a solo affair, and this is how you get colleagues to share a success or a problem with.

items.q: Which language does the community use, and do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: Our community language is English. Meetings and introductions are in English, and Spanish is welcome. You do not need to speak Spanish, and nobody is expected to speak both. Introductions through the time bank are in English, or in Spanish if that suits both people better.

items.q: I have just moved to Barcelona. Can I join?
items.a: Yes, if you are a founder, independent or senior professional based in the city. A trusted local network is the slowest thing to build when you arrive. Apply, tell us what you do, and you can meet members at co-working days and ask for introductions through the time bank.

items.q: How is Bizcelona different from Meetup or InterNations?
items.a: Open meetups and large expat networks are good for meeting many people. Bizcelona is built for the opposite: a small, approved group where every member has agreed to help, and where help carries on between events through the time bank rather than stopping when the room empties.
